System.IO is one of my favorite namespaces since I do a lot of work with files. Path, Directory, and File are some of my most used ‘utilitiy’ types (I coined the term for types with mostly static members).

For example, one common task is that I have a file path I want with a different extension.
private string ChangeFileExt(string FilePath, string NewExt)
{ return Path.Combine(Path.GetDirectoryName(FilePath), Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(FilePath) + "." + NewExt); }

Called with:
Trace.WriteLine(ChangeFileExt(@"c:tempexample.exe", "txt"));

One nice consistancy in the types, is that "Name" refers to just a file’s name (ex: Run.exe), "Path" refers to the whole path (ex: c:tempexample.exe), and "Directory" refers to the folder structure leading up to the path (c:temp). I can’t even count the number of times other devs I’ve worked with have used inconsistant member names which causes pain. They’ll call a property "FileName" and have the whole path. <sigh>
